en.title: Practice: Read Sentences in Chunks
en.summary: Learn how to pause at commas and adjust your voice tone when reading Romanian sentences in chunks.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: You group your words into chunks when you speak Romanian. A comma marks a pause between chunks. Your tone rises slightly at the comma. It shows that your thought is not finished yet. At the period, your pitch falls. This falling tone shows the end of the sentence.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Listen to (Mâine, merg la școală) /ˈmɨ.i.ne merɡ la ʃkoˈa.lə/. It means tomorrow I go to school. Raise your voice pitch slightly before the comma. Pause briefly at that mark. Then, say the second chunk and lower your tone.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: Every comma in a Romanian sentence creates a small border. You break long thoughts into easy parts at these marks. Never rush past a comma. Keep your voice tone high or level before the break. When you see a period, lower your tone firmly. The punctuation guides the music of your speech.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Many learners read a whole sentence in one flat breath. This makes speech sound mechanical and hard to follow. Do not drop your tone before the comma. A low tone signals that you want to stop talking. Also, do not pause between words that belong together. Only pause where you see punctuation.
